title: Ancient Wisdom. Modern Science.
intro: Wisdom transcends time, cultures, and traditions. At Golden Age, Dr. Hari Krishna brings together ancient Indian scriptures, teachings of spiritual masters from the East and West, and modern scientific perspectives to explore life's deepest questions. Through simple explanations and practical examples, he makes profound spiritual knowledge accessible to everyone, encouraging curiosity, awareness, and self-discovery.

cards.title: Ancient Scriptures & Timeless Teachings
cards.body: From the Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, Ashtavakra Gita, and Yoga Sutras to other sacred texts, Dr. Hari Krishna explores ancient wisdom in a way that connects with modern life. His teachings help seekers understand concepts such as karma, dharma, consciousness, self-realization, and the true nature of existence.

cards.title: Wisdom of Spiritual Masters
cards.body: Spiritual wisdom is not limited to one tradition or culture. Dr. Hari Krishna explores the teachings of great masters such as Buddha, Mahavatar Babaji, Adi Shankaracharya, Swami Vivekananda, Ramana Maharshi, and many others. Drawing from both Eastern and Western philosophies, he highlights different perspectives on meditation, awareness, inner transformation, and the search for truth.

cards.title: Where Science Meets Spirituality
cards.body: Can modern science help us understand ancient spiritual ideas? Dr. Hari Krishna explores the fascinating relationship between meditation, consciousness, neuroscience, psychology, physics, and spirituality. By examining scientific understanding alongside traditional spiritual teachings, he encourages deeper inquiry into the mind, body, energy, and human experience.

riverStory: A little boy once asked his grandfather, “Thatha, where do we go when we die?” The grandfather smiled: “To heaven, if we do good.” “But where is heaven, Thatha?” The grandfather had no answer — and the question never left the boy.
riverIntro: India's sages have walked with questions like that for over three thousand years. Their answers became the Vedas, the Upanishads, the Ramayana, the Mahabharata, the Gita and the Puranas. We grow up hearing these names — but rarely how they connect. Here is the secret: they are not a pile of separate books. They are one river, flowing from a mountain spring to the sea. Walk along it with us.

questions.label: Jagat-vichara
questions.title: What is this creation?
questions.body: Where did this world come from? Who sustains it? Is it real or a dream? Does it end — and what is my relationship to it?

questions.label: Atma-vichara
questions.title: How do I know myself?
questions.body: Who am I? Where did I come from, and where am I going? What is the purpose of my life, and how do I find lasting happiness?

questionsNote: These two questions set the river flowing. Every stage below answers them — in its own language.

stages.name: Shruti — the Vedas
stages.body: The rishis didn't write the mantras — they heard them, sitting in silence by forests and rivers. That is why the Vedas are called Shruti: “what was heard.” And the very first thing they heard was a question, full of wonder: what was there before anything was?
stages.verse: Nāsad āsīn no sad āsīt tadānīm
stages.meaning: Then there was neither non-being nor being.
stages.tryThis: Close your eyes for two minutes and just listen — every sound, near and far, without naming any of them. Listening was the first spiritual practice.

stages.place: Through the forest — deep and clear
stages.name: Vedanta — the Upanishads
stages.body: Then the river went quiet and deep. In forest hermitages, teachers whispered to students, and the question turned around. Not “what is the world?” but “who is the one asking?” The outer fire-ritual became an inner fire of inquiry.
stages.meaning: By whose will does the mind go forth?
stages.tryThis: The next time a thought arises, ask gently: “Who is aware of this thought?” Don't answer — just look.

stages.name: Smriti
stages.body: A truth that is only heard can be forgotten. So the sages remembered it — and retold it in words every generation could understand. Smriti is the bridge between the forest and the home.
stages.verse: Śrutis tu vedo vijñeyo dharma-śāstraṁ tu vai smṛtiḥ
stages.meaning: Shruti is the Veda; Smriti is the teaching of dharma.
stages.tryThis: Recall one value your grandparents lived by. Live by it once today.

stages.name: Itihasa — Ramayana & Mahabharata
stages.body: Now the river reached the people — Ayodhya, Mithila, Hastinapura, Kurukshetra. The Ramayana shows how to live; the Mahabharata teaches how to think when right and wrong are not black and white. Truth stopped being a sutra and became a person you could love.
stages.meaning: The epics and Puranas are the fifth Veda.
stages.tryThis: Facing a hard choice this week? Ask what dharma asks of you — not what is easiest.

stages.name: The Bhagavad Gita
stages.alias: Wisdom in the moment of crisis
stages.body: On a battlefield, a great warrior drops his bow and weeps. In that darkest moment, Krishna speaks — and the essence of every Upanishad pours into eighteen chapters. Crisis didn't stop the river. It made it deeper.
stages.meaning: The Self is never born and never dies.
stages.tryThis: Do one task today completely — and let go of how it turns out.

stages.name: The Puranas
stages.body: Finally the river split into a thousand streams and reached every village. A temple in every village, a story in every temple — and in every story, the same water. What only scholars understood, the Puranas sang to every heart.
stages.meaning: We meditate on the Supreme Truth.
stages.tryThis: Choose one Name and repeat it quietly for five minutes. No hurry, no comparison.

riverEnd: And where does the river end? In the ocean — and that ocean is your own heart. The whole journey was flowing toward you.
ghatsTitle: Which ghat will you step in from?
ghatsIntro: A river has many ghats — bathing steps — but the water is the same. The river never asks which steps you came down. Start wherever you are.

ghats.meaning: May that light inspire our understanding.

ghats.text: The Upanishad gives the great saying:
Rama's life shows the way; Yudhishthira's dilemmas teach discernment.

ghats.verse: Karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana
ghats.meaning: Your duty is in your hands — the fruit is not.

ghats.text: The Puranas give the path of love — hearing the story, singing the name, the heart melting into surrender.

closingMeaning: Truth is one; the wise speak of it in many ways.
closingBody: Because truth is one, the paths had to be many — that is not contradiction, it is compassion. Like a mother who sings to her baby, tells stories to her child and gives advice to her grown son: the language changes, the love does not. These are not six shelves in a library. They are six rooms in one heart — yours.
sourceNote: Adapted from the Telugu study “Bharatiya Jnana Parampara — from the Vedas to the Puranas, one living river.” Read the source texts yourself, find a teacher, and let one mantra walk with you.
libraryTitle: Explore the Golden Age Wisdom Library
libraryBody: Our vision is to make Golden Age a growing hub for spiritual knowledge — a place where anyone can discover ancient scriptures, learn about spiritual masters, explore different philosophies, and deepen their understanding. Through Dr. Hari Krishna's wisdom talks and educational resources, we aim to make this knowledge freely accessible to everyone.
libraryCloseSub: One place to discover wisdom from across the world.
